doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: Art Tatum: helping young players, intimidation and baseball
summary: Older New York musicians shared knowledge; Tatum got him the Stepin Fetchit gig and preferred talking baseball and pinochle.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Oh, New York was great because especially for a youngster trying to learn the music business. Because the older guys would show you everything, you know, whatever you asked, you couldn’t do it but they’d show you. I know I asked Tatum several times to show me certain things, he’d say, “Oh, Gerry,” [scats]. I’d say thanks.
But Art got me the gig with Stepin Fetchit.
Yeah he got me my first gig.
Was the average piano player intimidated by Art Tatum?

No, they just wished he’d go away, you know. One guy told me he says, “Wig, don’t worry about Art Tatum” he says, “much as he plays, he can only be in one place at one time, and he can’t work all the gigs all at once so you’re safe.” Which makes sense.

Art was really a sweetheart. He was a nice man, except he didn’t want to talk music, he wanted to talk baseball. You know he could tell you the average of Ty Cobb or anybody years before, you know? And how much they batted and what they did and all that. He was a good pinochle player too.
